Unfortunately this class was my biggest disappointment this semester. When the course is named "ways of seeing art and architectural history", I was expecting a lot more than the instructor making the students memorize a number of artifacts/artists. The general lectures were good and the instructor knows the subject but there are a number of improvements needed for this class. When an instructor makes participation to classes mandatory, I expect that there would be discussions in the class. The only time we were asked a question in the class was in one of the last weeks where he showed a building and asked us to try to figure out the style and timeframe from what we have learned in class. The class was strictly a lecture and I didn't learn anymore than I could by reading the textbook. The exams were also the continuation of his desire for us to memorize dates and artists, (which is perfectly fine for quizes if that is what he wants) which didn't leave any challenge or creative thinking on my side. I expected so much more from the class, exams and/or maybe research papers. Exams are also made up of memorizing the same things and the way that they are set up, student loses half of the exam because of time allocated for the identification of the various artifacts he shows on the screen one after the other. Then we are expected to write a whole essay and comparison questions in the limited time left again filled with dates etc. and one of the general comments he makes is that the essays are not as long or as detailed as he wants.. This can be an amazing introductory class that teaches everyone the evolution of art throughout history. I will try not to take anymore classes from this teacher if possible and I will stick to other classes where I will be challenged to learn instead of memorizing whatever the instructor wants us to memorize.

We are lucky to have a proffesional like Mr. Gates. Considering his experiences, it is a big plus for our country as well.

About the course, Charles does 6 quizzes, drops 2. But you have to memorize name, location, architects, and even the date of an artwork, which is pretty hard, especially in the exams, considering that there are almost hundreds of pictures. Maybe it is easy for a european or an american. They might remember, because even when they were children, they have the possibilities to visit many countries as easy as visiting any city of their country. However, as Turks, we don't even have any little idea about the general view of architecture of another country - due to visa issues or economy - so sometimes it is very hard for us to guess or memorize them, because those architectures are like from another world from our point of view :) But definetely you learn many, many things, and the most interesting one is the meanings, or the connections of the artworks, they all have stories. You wittness how styles have changed, how they affected each other, then how they came back. So it is indeed very interesting. Although I don't usually like observing artworks, nor going to the museums etc. , it was very joyful semester for me, so I would like to thank to Mr. Gates. 

In conclusion, apart from the hardships of being a Turk, one way or another, we need to have information about some artworks, at least the most famous ones, as a general knowladge. And this course provides it! And lastly, Mr. Gates gives our quizzes and the copy of our midterms exams back to us, so I can upload them to coursehero (I hope it does violate any rule). Probably it will be the first document in coursehero about HART117 in Bilkent, so you can easily unlock it ! I wish the best for all of you, Bilkenters ! Take care, Charles!
